subject: Stratagem RFP - availability measurement, latency targets, and crediting methodology

Subject: Clarification on uptime measurement and credits (RFP section 4.2)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the rapid submission of the RFP response. Our ops and legal teams reviewed section 4.2 — Availability, measurement and credits — and have a few clarifying questions so we can sign off internally:

1) Measurement sources: you list "synthetic probes + internal telemetry". Can you confirm which source is the primary datum for SLA calculations? If both are used, how do you reconcile discrepancies?

2) Windowing: the RFP asks for monthly availability. Do you compute availability on a rolling 30d window or calendar-month basis? Our billing runs on calendar months.

3) Latency: you provide p50/p95 latency targets for text generation. Are those based on per-request tail sampling or aggregated by customer route? How many samples per hour are required for the SLO to be considered valid?

4) Credits: please provide the exact formula for service credits and any caps/exclusions (maintenance, customer misconfiguration, DDoS).

Could you provide an annotated paragraph we can attach to our procurement worksheet and the legal team for redline review? Also flag any evidence artifacts we should expect (dashboards, raw telemetry, synthetic probe logs).

Appreciate it — Evan

--
Evan Cho
Senior Procurement Manager
Stratagem Systems

Legal will want precise language for exceptions (force majeure, scheduled maintenance, customer-configured routing, and documented integrator errors). Ops will need to attach dashboards and an evidence access plan.

I sketched an answer below that we can refine into an attachment (Stratagem_RFP_SLA_Response_v1.pdf). Please review for accuracy and sign-off.

Thanks — Rafa

> Draft (for edit):
> Redwood’s availability measurement is derived from a reconciliation of two independent telemetry sources: internal server-side request telemetry and externally-executed synthetic probes located in the customer’s preferred regions. For SLA calculation the canonical datum is the internal server-side successful-request count, with synthetic probes used as independent corroboration and for outage detection.
>
> Availability is computed on a calendar-month basis using successful request counts over total expected requests for that month. We also publish a rolling 30-day report for customers and internal ops, but contractual credits are assessed on the calendar month.
>
> Latency SLOs (p50/p95) are measured per-route using random sampling of live requests. By default we use continuous sampling at 1 request/sec per active route, with statistical aggregation to ensure at least 10k samples per 24-hour period for high-traffic routes; lower-volume routes use adaptive stratified sampling (minimum 100 samples/day) to avoid noisy percentiles.
>
> Service crediting: credits are issued as a percentage of monthly invoice for that billing month. Credit tiers: < 99.9%: 10% credit; 99.9–99.95%: 5% credit; >= 99.95%: no credit. Credits are subject to a monthly cap of 50% of the invoice for that month. Credits exclude downtime caused by customer misconfiguration, scheduled maintenance (≥72 hours advance notice for major planned maintenance; routine maintenance windows are excluded per section X), third-party infrastructure failure beyond Redwood control, and documented DDoS events demonstrated by traffic signatures.
>
> Evidence: synthetic probe dashboards (PNG exports), raw telemetry snapshots (CSV), request-level traces (redacted), and a signed incident post-mortem for any creditable outage.

--- BEGIN ANNOTATED RESPONSE ---
Redwood Inference — Availability measurement and crediting (summary)

1) Canonical measurement source: Redwood uses internal server-side successful-request telemetry (request accept + model response) as the canonical source for contractual SLA calculations. Externally-executed synthetic probes (customer-region probes) are maintained as an independent corroboration mechanism and for early detection of region-specific network anomalies. When internal telemetry and synthetic probes diverge materially (>0.5% discrepancy over a 1-hour window), an automatic reconciliation workflow is triggered and both datasets are retained for audit.

2) Windowing: availability is computed on a calendar-month basis for the purposes of service credits and billing. We also provide a rolling 30-day availability dashboard for operational visibility.

3) Latency SLOs and sampling: latency SLOs (p50/p95) are measured per-route. We employ continuous probabilistic sampling with an adaptive floor to ensure statistically meaningful percentiles: default continuous sampling at ~1 req/sec per active route and a minimum of 100/day for low-volume routes. High-traffic routes will have sample counts in the tens of thousands daily to stabilize tail estimates. Percentiles exclude requests affected by customer-provided erroneous payloads (HTTP 4xx validation errors) and known upstream timeouts.

4) Service credits: credits are calculated as a percentage of the affected calendar-month invoice using the following buckets: below 99.9% availability: 10% credit; 99.9%–99.95%: 5% credit; 99.95% and above: no credit. Credits are capped at 50% of the monthly invoice for any single month. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (with advance notice per contract), customer misconfiguration or misuse, third-party provider failures outside Redwood-managed infrastructure, and documented DDoS events validated by traffic signatures.

5) Evidence and audit artifacts: for any credit-eligible incident we provide: (a) synthetic probe dashboard exports (PNG), (b) raw telemetry snapshots (CSV) with timestamps and hashed request ids, (c) request-level trace samples with PII redacted, and (d) an incident post-mortem signed by Redwood on-call. Where requested under NDA we will provide extended logs and tooling access for agreed forensic analysis.

--- END ANNOTATED RESPONSE ---

Evan —

Appreciate the quick review. Short answers and delivery plan below:

1) Third-party examples and notifications: we will enumerate cloud-provider scenarios (control-plane API outages, regional AZ network partitions, managed DB failures) in the contract. For any qualifying third-party incident Redwood will: (a) notify the customer within 2 business hours of detection, (b) post a status update to the dedicated incident channel, and (c) include the third-party provider incident ID and timeline in the post-mortem.

2) Reconciliation: our reconciliation workflow is automated: when a >0.5% discrepancy is detected over a 1-hour rolling window an automated ticket is opened, data snapshots for both datasets are archived, and an on-call engineer performs triage. We retain both datasets for 12 months for audit. We can provide a redacted CSV export or S3 read-only bucket for forensic access under NDA for a defined retention window (default 30 days; extendable by agreement).

3) Evidence delivery and NDA: attached are the following artifacts (zipped and redacted): Playbook_oncall.pdf (on-call runbook and escalation matrix), Synthetic_Probe_Dashboards.png (PNG export of example probe dashboard), and a sanitized incident post-mortem sample in the PDF.
